info.title: Python TDD workflow with requirement-driven development

parts.text:
"You are inspecting a Python project inside a container at /app.

READ ONLY. Do not create, modify or delete any file under /app.
Any write there invalidates this run.

A developer is about to work on the task described below.

\"
<prompt>
    <role_setting>
        <identity>You are a senior programmer proficient in Python software engineering and Test-Driven Development (TDD).</identity>
        <expertise>You excel at implementing requirements and refactoring code in small-step iterations under a Test-Driven Development (TDD) workflow.</expertise>
        <scene>You are collaborating closely with a senior software architect. The architect produces incremental requirement documents based on the functional gaps of the current code; you are responsible for understanding the content of this document and implementing the requirements to change the status of target tests from non-passed to passed.</scene>
        <responsibilities>Your responsibilities are: Carefully read and understand the requirement document /app/requirement.xml, and modify the code according to the behavioral contracts defined in the document. You should follow the principle of necessary changes and avoid irrelevant modifications. You are prohibited from executing test actively.</responsibilities>
    </role_setting>

    <input>
        <permission>You are allowed to browse all content in the current working directory.</permission>
        <item name=\\"/app/code/\\">The folder containing all source code for this Python project.</item>
        <item name=\\"/app/code/tests/\\">The folder containing all unit tests for this Python project.</item>
        <item name=\\"/app/requirement.xml\\">The incremental requirement document provided by the architect (behavioral contract).</item>
    </input>

    <workflow>
        <rule>You must strictly follow the workflow below:</rule>
        <step index=\\"1\\" action=\\"read_requirements\\">
            Carefully read /app/requirement.xml to deeply understand every requirement (including the source code involved, current state, expected behavior, and acceptance criteria).
        </step>
        <step index=\\"2\\" action=\\"inspect_code\\">
            Based on the requirement list, carefully read the relevant code files in /app/code/ and understand their implementation. If necessary, you may consult the relevant test cases in /app/code/tests/ to understand the expected behavior.
        </step>
        <step index=\\"3\\" action=\\"implement\\">
            Based on the requirements and the current state of the code, consider the order of requirement implementation, formulate specific executable implementation plans for each requirement, and finally produce high-quality code implementations that comply with the contracts by directly editing the relevant code files.
        </step>
    </workflow>

    <constraints>
        <no_execution>You are strictly PROHIBITED from actively executing pytest, unittest, or any other test commands or scripts. Verification work is completed by an external system; you do not need to consider it.</no_execution>
        <operation>You are only allowed to modify or add content within the /app/code/ folder, excluding the tests subfolder. It is strictly PROHIBITED to make any changes to the /app/requirement.xml file or the /app/code/tests/ folder.</operation>
        <granularity>You must focus on the requirement document and only make necessary changes to satisfy the requirements. You should not expand the scope on your own or over-develop.</granularity>
    </constraints>

    <output>
        <product>Your modified codebase (changes under /app/code/). Briefly summarize your changes, but there is no need to create any new documentation files for this.</product>
    </output>
</prompt>

\"

Read enough of /app/code to answer concretely, then name 3 to 5
plausible FUTURE tasks that could reasonably follow this one in THIS codebase.
Refer to real files, functions or modules you actually read. Do not solve the
task, and do not write any file."

2: <requirement>
3:   <item>
4:     <location>/app/code/expression/core/builder.py</location>
5:     <description>The _send method in the base Builder class incorrectly handles async generators and StopIteration exceptions. It has improper handling of async generator yields and doesn't properly distinguish between StopIteration with values vs. StopIteration without values, leading to "Task got bad yield" and "coroutine raised StopIteration" errors.</description>
6:     <contract>Fix the _send method to properly handle async generators by correctly awaiting async values, properly differentiate between StopIteration with and without values, and correctly process async generator results.</contract>
7:     <acceptance>tests/test_async_result_builder.py::test_async_result_builder_return_ok, tests/test_async_result_builder.py::test_async_result_builder_yield_ok, tests/test_async_option_builder.py::test_async_option_builder_while</acceptance>
8:   </item>
9:   <item>
10:     <location>/app/code/expression/core/builder.py</location>
11:     <description>The base Builder class does not properly handle StopIteration exceptions that occur during synchronous generator processing, causing assertion failures in tests like test_result_builder_yield_from_ok and test_option_builder_yield_from_some.</description>
12:     <contract>Improve StopIteration handling in the _send method to correctly distinguish between StopIteration with values and StopIteration without values, and ensure proper propagation of values from StopIteration exceptions.</contract>
13:     <acceptance>tests/test_result_builder.py::test_result_builder_yield_from_ok, tests/test_option_builder.py::test_option_builder_yield_from_some</acceptance>
14:   </item>
15:   <item>
16:     <location>/app/code/expression/effect/result.py</location>
17:     <description>The ResultBuilder class implements a zero() method that returns Ok(None), but there are inconsistencies in how it's used and tested. Tests expect zero() to return specific values, but the implementation is incomplete.</description>
18:     <contract>Ensure the zero() method in ResultBuilder returns Ok(None) consistently and correctly handles empty generator scenarios in async contexts.</contract>
19:     <acceptance>tests/test_async_result_builder.py::test_async_result_builder_zero</acceptance>
20:   </item>
21:   <item>
22:     <location>/app/code/expression/effect/option.py</location>
23:     <description>The AsyncOptionBuilder class has issues with StopAsyncIteration handling that leads to AttributeError when trying to access .value attribute on StopAsyncIteration exceptions.</description>
24:     <contract>Fix StopAsyncIteration handling in AsyncOptionBuilder._send to properly handle the absence of .value attribute and correctly process generator termination.</contract>
25:     <acceptance>tests/test_async_option_builder.py::test_async_option_builder_zero</acceptance>
26:   </item>
27:   <item>
28:     <location>/app/code/expression/core/builder.py</location>
29:     <description>The base Builder class doesn't properly handle the case where generators return None (StopIteration without a value) in the main execution loop, causing it to call zero() incorrectly.</description>
30:     <contract>Improve the main execution loop in the __call__ method to properly detect when a generator has yielded None and should call zero() instead of attempting to bind/combine results.</contract>
31:     <acceptance>tests/test_result_builder.py::test_result_builder_yield_from_ok, tests/test_option_builder.py::test_option_builder_yield_from_some</acceptance>
32:   </item>
33: </requirement>
